record.original_question: Can one rigorously prove universality for one of the other numerical algorithms with random data discussed in the paper, especially the conjugate-gradient algorithm for solving a random linear system A x = b with both A and b random?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting and challenging open problem to prove universality rigorously for any of the other numerical algorithms discussed in [40]. The conjugate gradient algorithm, in particular, to compute the solution of the linear system Ax = b with A and b random, seems to be "within reach".

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ be a random symmetric positive-definite matrix (for example, a sample covariance / Wishart matrix $A = \frac{1}{m} X X^{T}$ with $X$ an $n \times m$ matrix of i.i.d. entries having mean $0$, variance $1$, and sufficient moment conditions, with $m/n \to \gamma > 1$), and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ be an independent random vector with i.i.d. entries (mean $0$, variance $1$). Apply the conjugate gradient algorithm to solve the linear system $A x = b$, starting from $x_{0} = 0$, and define the halting time
$$\tau_{n}(\varepsilon) \;=\; \min\bigl\{ k \geq 1 \;:\; \|r_{k}\| / \|r_{0}\| < \varepsilon \bigr\},$$
where $r_{k} = b - A x_{k}$ is the $k$-th residual and $\varepsilon > 0$ is a fixed tolerance.

Empirically, the fluctuations of $\tau_{n}(\varepsilon)$ — that is, $(\tau_{n}(\varepsilon) - \mathbb{E}\tau_{n}(\varepsilon))/\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}\,\tau_{n}(\varepsilon)}$ — converge as $n \to \infty$ to a limiting distribution that depends only on $\gamma$ and $\varepsilon$, and not on the distribution of the entries of $X$ and $b$ (a universality phenomenon).

Problem: Prove rigorously this universality statement for the conjugate gradient algorithm. More precisely, establish a limit theorem (e.g., a central limit theorem) for $\tau_{n}(\varepsilon)$, or for a closely related observable such as $\|r_{k}\|$, showing that the limiting law is independent of the underlying entry distribution within a broad class.
artifact.category_tag: Universality for numerical algorithms on random matrices
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Paquette and Trogdon proved a central limit theorem and a four-moment universality result for the residuals of the conjugate gradient and MINRES algorithms applied to sample covariance matrices, implying an almost-deterministic halting time. Deift–Trogdon and related work show that on well-conditioned Wishart matrices the CG halting time is almost deterministic. However, fully general universality results for the halting-time distribution across broad random-matrix ensembles and data distributions are not yet completely established, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Universality for the conjugate gradient and MINRES algorithms on sample covariance matrices
status_evidence.snippet: A central limit theorem is proved for norms of the residual vectors produced by the conjugate gradient and MINRES algorithms... a four moment theorem for the spectral measure that implies universality for the Lanczos iteration matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Universality and CLT for CG/MINRES residuals on sample covariance matrices have been proved.

status_evidence.title: The conjugate gradient algorithm on well-conditioned Wishart matrices is almost deterministic
status_evidence.snippet: Proof that the halting time is almost deterministic, relying on rigidity, delocalization and edge universality of random matrices.
status_evidence.claim: On well-conditioned Wishart matrices, CG halting time is shown to be almost deterministic.

status_evidence.title: Smoothed Analysis for the Conjugate Gradient Algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Smoothed analysis results for CG on random data.
status_evidence.claim: Further rigorous probabilistic analysis of CG on random inputs has been carried out.
